description:
Batch file renaming utility for Windows and Mac.

Advanced Renamer is a program for renaming multiple files and folders at once. By configuring renaming methods the names can be manipulated in various ways.
It is easy to set up a batch rename using multiple methods on a large amount of files. The 13 different methods enables you to change the names, and timestamps of files in one go. The files can also be copied or moved to new locations based on information in the files.
With Advanced Renamer you can construct new file names by adding, removing, replacing, changing case, or giving the file a brand new name based on known information about the file.
Before performing the operations on the files you can verify that the output will be correct and if you perform the rename and regret it, you can undo the complete batch.
Saved method lists are now batch projects

Batch methods are now saved together with batch settings in a project, making it easier to reuse the whole configuration in a consistent workflow. Existing .aren batch method files still work and new projects are also backwards compatible, but will contain more project specific configuration.

The new Project Settings window lets you override renaming settings for the current project only, such as word separators, zero padding, and the replacement for unsupported characters. The three new features of batch projects, Named counters, Project tags, and Custom filename validation, are also available in the Project settings window.

Named counters, referenced with tags like <Inc Nr:Name> are used for keeping track of numeric sequences within the project across multiple program sessions. When a batch is completed, the named counters are updated and their numeric values are preserved for the next batch, so that the next batch can continue the sequence seamlessly.

Project tags, referenced with <Project Name>, are used for values you want to reuse throughout the project. The value can be both a static value and it can be a dynamic value derived from a series of other tags.

For more advanced repeated workflows, set up a filename validation to catch potential naming issues before they occur. A filename validation can enforce rules such as required regex patterns and specific length constraints for filenames.

To make room for batch project controls and keep them grouped together, the main toolbar has been reorganized. Loading and saving projects should also feel more natural now.

Note: Named counters and Project tags, and Filename validation are only available for licensed users.

Tags reorganization

To make it easier to find the right tag, the tags from the categories Default, Advanced, File size, and Checksum, have been reorganized into Filename, Number, Data, and File info.

Tags of Filename category:
<Name>, <Ext>, <FolderName>, <SubFolder>, <Word>, <RWord>, <SubStr>, <RSubStr>, <Switch>

Tags of Number category:
<Inc Nr>, <Dec Nr>, <Inc NrDir>, <Inc Alpha>, <Inc Hex>, <Inc Roman>, <Rand>, <Rand Str>, <Num Files>, <Num Dirs>, <Num Items>, and any named counter tags.

Tags of Data category:
<ExifTool>, <->, <Csv>, <MediaType>, and any custom project tags.

Tags of File info category:
<Filesize>, <MD5>, <SHA1>

The documentation has been updated to reflect the new categories.

Copy/Paste batch method configuration

You can now copy the configuration from one batch method and paste it into another method of the same type. Select the source method and choose "Copy configuration" from the method header right click menu, then select the destination method and choose "Paste configuration" from the same menu to reuse its settings.

Batch method condition enhancements

When using Equals, Contains, Starts with, or Ends with, you can now enter a list of values to match. This lets one condition match several alternatives, such as applying a method to files with any of several extensions, without writing a regular expression.

You can also use any metadata field as the condition field. This makes it possible to decide whether a method should be applied based on information stored in the file, such as an artist or camera model, in addition to its name, extension, or path.

Full list of changes in version 4.26
- Method lists are now called Batch Projects
- Added Project Settings window
- UI: Reorganized the main toolbar to make room for functionality related to Batch Project
- Tags: Reorganized some tags into new categories: Default, Advanced, File size, Checksum has become Filename, Number, Data, File info
- Main window: All panel headers now have a right click menu to quickly change various UI settings
- Main window: Dragging a .aren file to the main window will load the method list instead of adding it to the item list
- List: Columns can now be dragged to a new location in the list and in the customize columns window
- Batch method: Copy/Paste configuration between methods of the same type
- New case method: Added two new options, "Apply Lowercase first" and "Ignore words in all caps", available for some configurations
- Batch method condition: Pattern can now be a list of values when match type Equals, Contains, Starts with, or Ends with is used
- Batch method condition: Any metadata field can be used as a condition field
- UpDown arrow buttons in methods now behave more predictably
